newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end stronger, spreads reach new lows.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end stronger, spreads reach new lows.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Wednesday, with spreads to U.S. long bonds reaching new lows, as foreign buying and tame Canadian economic data pushed prices higher, analysts said.

"Bonds are still rallying on the back of the Fed not going the other day plus the positive data today. It was pretty straightfoward, guys covering some of their shorts," said Garett Prins, a fixed-income analyst with J.P. Morgan Canada.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.18 to C$112.00 to yield 6.992 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 24/32 to yield of 6.96 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to three basis points, a new low, from 11 basis points at Tuesday's close.

Canadian bonds began rallying on Tuesday along with the Canadian dollar after the U.S. Federal Reserve announced its decision to hold rates steady. There had been concern a U.S. rate hike would weigh on the Canadian dollar, which in turn would hurt bonds.
The Canadian bond market received further support this morning from a retail sales report which showed sales unexpectedly fell in March.

"The retail sales number certainly was a bit of a surprise, it was a little soft. That may have provided some more support to the long end of the market," said David Yu, a fixed-income portfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc.
Yu said strong buying by foreigners in a relatively illiquid market may have been the reason for the dramatic narrowing of spreads.
In new issue news, the Bank of Canada will release details on Thursday of the Government of Canada's auction of five-year bonds on May 28.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.09 to C$103.87 to yield 6.449 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 13/32 to yield 6.73 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds widened to 28 basis points from 21 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.93 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.12 percent.
